metadata.title: Are students trying hard to succeed in PISA?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA in Focus brief uses PISA 2018 results and reports standardized disengagement measures across countries/economies. The document does not specify whether analysts applied student sampling weights or replicate weights in the production of the reported cross-country comparisons, so the exact weighting variable(s) are not extractable from the text. The brief also does not describe any plausible-value (PV) estimation workflow, but it does interpret relationships between disengagement indicators and PISA reading performance after accounting for student characteristics (e.g., gender and socio-economic status), implying that PISA’s standard scaling/estimation approach was used in the underlying OECD analyses. For replication, analysts should use the OECD/PISA 2018 database documentation for complex survey design and scaling, and apply the recommended weights when estimating country comparisons and regression-based associations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This brief is a policy brief summarizing descriptive and association results from PISA 2018 rather than reporting an explicit PV-based achievement modeling pipeline in the text provided. The outcomes emphasized here are disengagement indicators (self-reported effort, rapid guessing, and questionnaire non-response) and their associations with reading performance, but the document does not report the PV estimation/combining procedure used for reading scores. Missing-data handling is therefore not documented at the level required to classify a specific imputation/deletion strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The brief reports PISA 2018 results and compares disengagement measures across participating countries/economies. It does not specify an analytic subsample restriction beyond the fact that rapid guessing is only available for countries/economies that administered the computer-based assessment. The reported associations with reading performance are described as accounting for student characteristics (e.g., gender and socio-economic status), but no further inclusion/exclusion rules or complete-case criteria are stated in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA in Focus brief uses PISA 2018 to examine student disengagement under low-stakes conditions, focusing on three measures: self-reported effort (effort thermometer, inverted to reflect disengagement), rapid guessing (share of responses under five seconds in the computer-based assessment), and questionnaire non-response (share of missing questionnaire items). The brief reports that consistency between these measures is low, suggesting that disengagement is multi-dimensional and should not be captured by a single indicator. Across countries/economies, boys show higher disengagement than girls, with larger gaps for behavioural measures than for self-reported effort. Higher disengagement is associated with lower reading performance across measures, with stronger relationships for behavioural indicators than for self-reported effort; rapid guessing is more closely related to performance than non-response. The brief also notes that causal direction is not straightforward because disengagement and performance can influence each other, and it highlights a Spain comparability concern due to timing overlap with high-stakes exams.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a policy brief summarizing descriptive and association results from PISA 2018 rather than an empirical machine-learning study with a documented predictive modeling pipeline. As a result, there are no extractable ML algorithms, PV-handling procedures, missing-data handling strategy, or student-level analytic sample sizes in the provided text. The extraction therefore treats the document as an assessment/interpretation brief rather than a predictive research paper.
